title: People of the UK: London Case Study

concepts.def: UK capital and global city of ~9 million people.
Major hub for finance, culture and decision making worldwide.
Square Mile financial district with banks and the Bank of England.
Over 300 languages spoken; ~40% born outside the UK.
Elizabeth Line opened in 2022, cutting east-west journey times.
Boroughs like Kensington sit next to poorer ones like Tower Hamlets. 🏙

walkthroughs.body_html:
Greater London houses about 9 million people.

It is a global city, alongside New York and Tokyo.

Hosts the headquarters of many TNCs.

It is incredibly diverse.

Over 300 languages are spoken across the city.

Roughly 40% of residents were born outside the UK.

Transport keeps changing.

The Elizabeth Line (Crossrail) opened in 2022.

It boosted east-west capacity by around 10%.

mcqs.q: Why do meanders migrate across a floodplain?
options: Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
The Brandt Line is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Meanders form because rivers flow around obstacles like rocks.
Faster water on the outside of the bend causes erosion (river cliff); slower water on the inside causes deposition (slip-off slope) — over time the channel shifts laterally.

mcqs.q: Why is the Brandt Line considered outdated?
options: The Brandt Line is the boundary between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.
Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
The Brandt Line still accurately divides rich and poor countries today.
Drawn in 1980, it predates the rise of NICs (China, India, Brazil) and globalisation — countries like South Korea, Singapore and Chile no longer fit neatly on the 'poor south' side.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between the focus and epicentre of an earthquake?
options: Meanders form because the river is going downhill very steeply.
The focus is at the centre of the Earth and the epicentre is on the surface.
The focus (hypocentre) is the underground point where the earthquake originates; the epicentre is the point on the surface directly above the focus.
The focus and epicentre are the same point.
